title: Quarter-wave initialized 22-layer HfO2/SiO2 multi-cavity with phase-matched seeding
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses at theoretical quarter-wave optical thickness (QWOT) centered at 267.5 nm will align the fundamental stopband transition with the target UV passband from optimization start, reducing optimizer steps needed to resolve sharp passband edges and improving early-round score convergence compared to uniform 50 nm initialization.
design_principle: Multi-cavity defect structure with alternating high/low index layers, where initial thicknesses are seeded at QWOT values (HfO2 ~33.4 nm, SiO2 ~46.5 nm) at the geometric center of the 255-280 nm passband. The symmetric unit cell approach creates stopbands with high reflectivity while maintaining transmissivity in the target passband.
proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2/SiO2]_11 | Fused silica substrate (22 finite layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Initialized at QWOT: HfO2 layers ~33.4 nm, SiO2 layers ~46.5 nm
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 may form uneven surfaces during evaporation per evidence
Thickness tolerance sensitivity should be evaluated
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: optical thickness = λ/4n produces constructive interference for reflection at design wavelength
Multi-cavity defect resonance: introducing phase defects in periodic stack creates transmission passband within stopband
Symmetric unit cell (L/2 H L/2) approach from photonic crystal filter literature
expected_advantages: Phase-matched initialization reduces optimization iterations to reach high-quality local optimum
QWOT seeding aligns stopband edges with visible/NIR suppression bands from start
Maintains proven 22-layer topology from route_04 while improving convergence behavior
known_risks: HfO2 surface unevenness may cause thickness inhomogeneity per evidence
QWOT initialization may trap optimizer in different local optimum than uniform initialization
22 layers may be insufficient for broad visible/NIR blocking with sharp UV passband
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | Fused silica. Initialize all HfO2 layer thicknesses at 33.4 nm and all SiO2 layer thicknesses at 46.5 nm (quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5 nm). Optimize all 22 thicknesses with bounds 20-300 nm using gradient-based optimizer. Objective: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm band, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm bands. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Evaluate spectral performance across 250-1150 nm. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 255–280 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Transmittance in 300–700 nm; Transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers; No metal layers; Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directive to reinitialize thicknesses at theoretical QWOT values (HfO2 ~33.4 nm, SiO2 ~46.5 nm at λ=267.5 nm) to align stopband transition with target window from optimization start, reducing optimizer steps needed for sharp passband edges.
